result.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
result.summary: Language agents increasingly work for users on the open Web, and finance is where trusting them is hardest. The data must come from the Web, the strategy lives in the user's head, and correctness depends on time, so an agent can fail silently: a strategy the user never asked for, unverified data, or a backtest that uses the future yields a report as convincing as a correct one. Existing benchmarks close the world somewhere, fixing the task, the data, or the timeline, and thereby remove these failures instead of measuring them. We introduce FINCOSMOS, an open-world evaluation paradigm for agents doing financial work. A simulated user holds a hidden strategy sampled from a compositional grammar and reveals it only when asked. The agent receives no data, so it must acquire data from the Web, build its own backtest under a data cutoff, and deliver verifiable results. Grading needs no reference answer. Programs verify point-in-time correctness and recompute every reported metric, the delivered strategy is checked against the hidden specification, and a run is accepted only when the user is satisfied and none of 15 veto checks fails. Across four coding agents and a model without tools in 150 sessions, no session is accepted: every session that the simulated user signed off fails a program check, and agents raise only 54--64\% of the details they were not told. Human experts attribute 88.33\% of failures to the agents. With FINCOSMOS feedback, an agent with persistent memory learned all ten tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FINCOSMOS：一个面向金融任务 agent 的开放世界评测范式，用户隐藏策略、agent 须自行从网络取数并在时间切点下自建可验证回测，由程序做时点正确性核查与指标重算，无参考答案评分。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉主线无直接关系，但其“何时向用户追问、自行取证据、程序化判定何时可交付”的设置，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据获取与停止决策的评价设计提供概念参照，值得核查。
